name: COLT (COllaborative Learning-based Tool Retrieval)
venue: CIKM 2024 (Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management, pp. 1930-1940); arXiv:2405.16089 (v1 May 2024, v2 Jul 2024)
authors_affiliation: Changle Qu, Sunhao Dai, Jun Xu, Ji-Rong Wen (Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China); Xiaochi Wei, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin (Baidu Inc.); Hengyi Cai (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences). Corresponding/lead institution: Renmin University of China.
code_url: https://github.com/quchangle1/COLT (also HuggingFace https://huggingface.co/Tool-COLT for processed ToolBench data and first-stage checkpoints; ToolLens dataset released in the repo)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/quchangle1/COLT (repo hosts code + ToolLens dataset; not a continuously-updated leaderboard, last commit Nov 2024)
task_domain: tool-use (tool retrieval for tool-augmented LLMs); information retrieval (cs.IR / cs.CL)
problem_setting: Offline, single-step tool retrieval for tool-augmented LLMs: given a (typically short, multifaceted) user query and a large static tool set, retrieve a top-K subset of tools so that the LLM can answer. Supervision is available (query-to-ground-truth-tool-set labels) and the retriever is trained in two supervised stages (semantic learning then graph collaborative learning). It is not an interactive agent loop; retrieval happens once per query before LLM tool use. Single-agent. The work emphasizes recovering the COMPLETE set of diverse tools a multifaceted query needs rather than ranking similar tools.
what_is_retrieved: tools (tool/API descriptions). Each tool is a (tool, description) pair; ground truth for a query is a small complete set of 1-4 collaborative tools.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus of tools/APIs (a fixed tool set of size N, e.g. 464 tools for ToolLens). No agent-written growing memory; the retrievable store is frozen after offline training.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-oriented: the explicit goal is to recover the complete minimal set of multiple diverse collaborative tools a query needs (multi-tool completeness), not a fixed semantic top-k of similar tools. The paper introduces the COMP@K metric measuring whether the full ground-truth tool set is contained in the top-K, and a list-wise multi-label loss that treats the whole ground-truth tool set as one entity. Output is still a top-K list (K in {3,5}), but optimized for set completeness.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; only Retrieve-like behavior, no Reuse/Revise/Retain of cases)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is a graph-collaborative-learning dense tool retriever.
retrieval_unit: tool-API (a single tool described by its textual description). Ground-truth target is a complete set of such tool-API units (a 'scene' = the group of collaborative tools for a query).
index_source: Static corpus: a fixed tool set indexed offline. Query/tool/scene embeddings are induced offline via two-stage training (PLM semantic fine-tuning + LightGCN graph collaborative learning on training-set bipartite graphs); no online/test-time growth of the store.
index_structure_topology: Graph-structured: three bipartite graphs among queries, scenes, and tools - Query-Scene (Q-S), Query-Tool (Q-T), and Scene-Tool (S-T). A 'scene' node aggregates the ground-truth tool set of a query, giving a hierarchical query->scene->tool topology that captures high-order inter-tool collaborative relationships. Underlying tool embeddings live in a flat dense vector space; the collaborative structure is the bipartite-graph overlay.
retriever_type: Hybrid learned dense retriever: PLM bi-encoder (dense) backbone + graph neural network (LightGCN) collaborative-learning layer on top. Model-agnostic over dense backbones (ANCE, TAS-B, coCondenser, Contriever). BM25 is used only as a baseline, not a component.
retriever_learning_signal: Learned/supervised in two stages: (1) Semantic learning - contrastive InfoNCE on query-positive-tool vs negative-tool pairs (similarity labels). (2) Collaborative learning - a list-wise multi-label loss (cross-entropy between ideal vs predicted selection distributions over a sampled tool list, treating the whole ground-truth set jointly) plus a cross-view InfoNCE contrastive loss aligning scene-centric and tool-centric query/scene representations. No RL, no LM-feedback reward; trained on ground-truth tool-set labels.
query_construction: Raw user query is encoded directly (mean-pooled PLM embedding) as the query key; no decomposition, expansion, or thought-conditioning. Collaborative refinement of the query representation is then done via graph message propagation (the query node aggregates from its scene/tool neighbors during training).
query_granularity: task-level (one query, one-shot at retrieval time). The dual-view design retrieves via two representations (scene-centric e_q^S and tool-centric e_q^T) but both are computed at the single-query level.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (single retrieval pass per query before LLM tool use; no iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is performed once per query unconditionally before tool use; there is no learned or confidence-based trigger.
reranking: No separate cross-encoder reranking stage. Final ranking is by a combined matching score y_hat(q,t) = sim(e_q^S, e_t^T) + sim(e_q^T, e_t^T) that fuses the scene-centric and tool-centric views; this dual-view scoring is collaborative/scene-aware but is the primary scorer, not a second-stage reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: none (no post-retrieval distillation/compression of tool descriptions). Refinement happens in the representation space during training (graph propagation, contrastive alignment), not as a post-retrieval filtering step on the returned list.
tool_document_engineering: Tool descriptions are used largely as raw text encoded by the PLM bi-encoder (mean pooling of the final layer). The novelty is not in document expansion but in the 'scene' abstraction: ground-truth tool sets are grouped into scene nodes whose embedding is the mean pooling of member-tool embeddings. ToolLens construction uses GPT-4 scene mining and query rewriting to build queries, but tool docs themselves are not synthetically augmented.
index_content_separation: N/A (no progressive-disclosure / index-then-content separation; tool descriptions are the retrievable units directly).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (fixed tool set, e.g. 464 tools filtered from ToolBench/RapidAPI for ToolLens). No live CRUD synchronization or MCP integration; tools originate from the RapidAPI-based ToolBench collection but the retrieval index is offline/static.
tool_dependency_awareness: Yes - this is the central contribution. COLT models inter-tool collaborative relationships (tools that must be used together to fully answer a multifaceted query) via the 'scene' concept and three bipartite graphs (Q-S, Q-T, S-T) with LightGCN message propagation, capturing high-order collaborative/dependency structure rather than treating tools independently. It models collaborative co-usage rather than explicit data-flow dependencies (output-of-A feeds B) or shared-auth prerequisites.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved top-K tools (their descriptions) are provided to the LLM, which then uses them to generate a response (validated in the downstream tool-learning study where retrieved top-3 tools feed GPT-4). The retriever itself is trained with the list-wise + contrastive objective; the retrieved tools are not adapted/revised before use.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan / one-shot at plan time: tools are retrieved once up front and supplied to the LLM, which then plans and acts with them. No interleaving of retrieval inside a planning/search loop; tool retrieval is a front-end module decoupled from the LLM's reasoning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (retrieval done once for the whole query/answer; not woven per CoT step or per tool call).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; retrieved tools are passed to the LLM as-is).
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form injected to the LLM is the raw tool/API descriptions of the top-K retrieved tools (plus implicitly their callable signatures for downstream tool use). Internally tools are dense embeddings refined by graph collaborative learning.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool/API (a concrete callable function with its description); the retrieval target is the complete set of such tools, conceptually grouped under a higher-level 'scene' abstraction during learning.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Indirect: the cross-view graph contrastive learning and list-wise multi-label loss promote balanced, scene-aware representations so that semantically-similar-but-redundant tools are not over-retrieved and complementary tools are recovered; semantic learning stage uses contrastive negatives. There is no explicit relevance-evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-filtering module on the retrieved output.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory; static tool corpus with learned embeddings).
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases; it is trained offline and the tool store is fixed at inference.
online_growth: No. The retrievable tool store and learned graphs are frozen after offline training; no growth during deployment.
failure_experience_usage: N/A / success-only-style supervision: training uses ground-truth positive tool sets and (randomly sampled / contrastive) negative tools, but there is no storage or retrieval of failed execution experiences; failures are not used as a corrective memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate; embeddings are fixed after training).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: retrieval is a learned model (trained dense + GNN retriever with list-wise/contrastive objectives) rather than off-the-shelf top-k similarity, but it is NOT an RL/Q-learning policy - it is a supervised ranking model. Selection at inference is still argtop-K over the learned matching score.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-retriever, single-agent setting; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: ToolLens (newly introduced; 18,770 queries, 464 tools, 1-3 tools/query); ToolBench subsets I2 (82,507 queries-ish stats: 74,257 train / 8,250 test, 11,473 tools, 2-4 tools/query) and I3 (21,361 train / 2,373 test, 1,419 tools, 2-4 tools/query). TOOLE is discussed as a prior dataset (used in dataset-quality comparison, not as a retrieval test set).
baselines: BM25 (lexical); dense PLM retrievers ANCE, TAS-B, coCondenser (coCondensor), Contriever - each evaluated Zero-shot and +Fine-tune; COLT is applied on top of each dense backbone (+COLT). Backbone-size study spans BERT-mini to BERT-large.
key_metrics: Recall@K (R@K), NDCG@K (N@K) for K in {3,5}; and the newly proposed COMP@K (C@K) completeness metric = fraction of queries whose full ground-truth tool set is contained in the top-K. Further analysis also uses Recall@|N| and COMP@|N| (K set to the number of ground-truth tools). Downstream: GPT-4 pairwise Elo ratings over Coherence/Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Overall.
headline_result: On ToolLens, Contriever+COLT reaches R@3 93.64 / R@5 97.75 / N@3 94.53 / C@3 84.55 (vs Contriever+Fine-tune R@3 83.58 / C@3 59.46), i.e. ~+25 absolute on COMP@3. Most-cited headline: BERT-mini (11M) equipped with COLT outperforms BERT-large (340M, 30x larger) without COLT. Largest gains are on the COMP (completeness) metric across all backbones and datasets.
ablations: Table 5 ablates four components on ToolLens and ToolBench(I3) using R@|N| and C@|N|: (1) w/o semantic learning -> catastrophic drop (e.g. ANCE+COLT C@|N| 78.36 -> 6.84), confirming semantic fine-tuning is the foundation; (2) w/o collaborative learning (semantic only) -> large drop (78.36 -> 49.01), showing graph collaborative learning drives completeness; (3) w/o list-wise learning (pairwise instead) -> notable drop (78.36 -> 52.68), showing list-wise multi-label loss is key to completeness; (4) w/o contrastive learning (no cross-view InfoNCE) -> drop (78.36 -> 63.87), especially impactful for Contriever. Also: model-size study (BERT-mini..BERT-large), per-tool-count subset analysis (gains largest for 3-4 tool queries), and hyperparameter analysis on tau, lambda, list length L.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@K, NDCG@K, and the completeness metric COMP@K) are reported separately from the downstream end-to-end tool-learning quality (GPT-4 pairwise Elo on generated responses), explicitly decoupling retrieval quality from generation quality.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both: intrinsic retrieval-process quality (Recall/NDCG/COMP completeness of the retrieved tool set) plus downstream outcome quality of LLM responses (Elo over Coherence/Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Overall). The completeness metric itself is a process-quality measure of the retrieved set.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Parameter/efficiency emphasis: COLT lets a tiny BERT-mini (11M) beat BERT-large (340M, 30x more params), and is model-agnostic so it boosts small backbones cheaply. The motivation is reducing LLM input length/latency by retrieving a small complete tool set instead of inputting all tools. No explicit per-query latency or API-cost numbers are reported for the retriever itself; LightGCN adds lightweight propagation over a frozen graph.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: top-K with K in {3,5} for main retrieval evaluation, and K=|N| (number of ground-truth tools) in the further analysis. The downstream study uses top-3 retrieved tools fed to GPT-4. The list-wise loss samples a tool list of length L (containing N_q positives + L-N_q sampled negatives) during training. No adaptive/precision-driven variable-size selection at inference.
benchmark_construction_and_size: ToolLens: 18,770 queries over 464 callable tools (filtered from ToolBench/RapidAPI, excluding auth/test tools), each query mapped to 1-3 verified tools; 10% held out as test (1,877 test queries). Constructed via a 5-step GPT-4 pipeline with human verification at each step: tool selection, scene mining, query generation, tool aggregation (multi-tool), and query rewriting - designed to produce concise, natural, multifaceted queries (verified superior to ToolBench/TOOLE by GPT-4 and human eval). ToolBench (I2, I3) reused as additional benchmarks. Best-system difficulty signal: on ToolLens COMP@3 only reaches ~84.55 (Contriever+COLT) and on ToolBench(I3) COMP@3 ~52, showing complete multi-tool retrieval remains hard.
builds_on: Dense retrieval bi-encoders (ANCE, TAS-B, coCondenser, Contriever) and the BEIR framework for semantic learning; LightGCN graph collaborative filtering for the collaborative-learning stage; InfoNCE contrastive learning; ToolBench / RapidAPI tool collection for tools and as a benchmark. Tool-learning context: ToolLLaMA, ToolBench (Qin et al. 2023b).
contrasts_with: Standard semantic-matching dense tool retrievers that rank tools by query-description similarity (the paper argues these retrieve redundant/similar tools and miss complementary ones), BM25 lexical retrieval, and traditional retrieval metrics (Recall, NDCG) that ignore set completeness. Also contrasts with recommendation/semantic-search settings that select any relevant items without modeling collaborative tool utility.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): tool retrieval line. A 2024 milestone reframing tool retrieval from per-tool semantic ranking to completeness/collaboration-oriented set recovery (introduces 'scene', bipartite-graph collaborative learning, the COMP@K metric, and the ToolLens benchmark); precursor to later dependency-aware / completeness-aware tool retrieval and to the authors' subsequent tool-learning survey work.
